Any passage that mentions <term>YHVH Elohim</term> <gloss>The Lord God</gloss> refers to actions performed through the completion of all attributes, both the attribute of Justice and the attribute of Mercy. This is what you find regarding the creation of the first man, his judgment, and his expulsion, and in all those matters. You will find that they all came about through both the attribute of Justice and the attribute of Mercy, and everything was in perfect completion, with mercy and justice as was fitting in true judgment. According to this principle, the Torah says: "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>original: "הצור תמים פעלו"</note>. The explanation of the verse is this: The Rock, who decrees judgment with strength, does not act with cruelty; He only decrees judgment after consulting both attributes, Loving-kindness and Justice. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect" <note>clarification: the word for perfect, *tamim*, implies this union</note>. For the expression <term>tamim</term> <gloss>perfect/complete</gloss> is the secret of two things, as if it said <term>te'omim</term> <gloss>twins</gloss>. However, in language of honor, it uses the term *tamim* for two things above, and the term *te'omim* for those below. Thus it says: "And they shall be coupled <note>original: "תאומים" (twins/coupled)</note> together beneath, and they shall be complete <note>original: "תמים"</note> together above his head." Below they are twins; above they are perfect. This is because below they appear as two things—a thing and its opposite, like a supporter and an accuser—but above everything is one intention. Whether it is the supporter or the accuser, both have one single intent. There is no hatred or love there, and no favoritism, only true judgment. Therefore it says "His work is perfect," for He consulted Justice and Mercy and then decreed the judgment; this is the secret of true judgment. And regarding what is said, "For all His ways are justice," the explanation is that everything is visible to the eye of every observer, as it says, "For all His ways are justice." 

You already know that Justice is comprised of both Judgment and Mercy, for Justice corresponds to Jacob, who is the "middle line" that mediates between the two tents, which are Abraham and Isaac. Abraham corresponds to <term>Hesed</term> <gloss>Loving-kindness</gloss>; Isaac corresponds to <term>Din</term> <gloss>Justice/Judgment</gloss>; Jacob decides between them, "a simple man, dwelling in tents." Justice corresponds to Jacob, drawing from Loving-kindness on Abraham's side and from Justice on Isaac's side. Thus it says, "You have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob." And the Prophet said, "O Lord, correct me, but with justice; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing." The explanation of the verse "O Lord, correct me, but with justice" is that the word <term>akh</term> <gloss>but/only</gloss> acts as a partition, meaning: with only half of the attribute of Justice, which is the Loving-kindness. For Justice is half judgment and half kindness. Therefore it says "but with justice," and afterwards says "not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing." He revealed the secret of diminishing the half of Justice that comes from the side of anger. Therefore, Justice is dependent upon Jacob, who is the "Father of the Tribes"; having known the great pain of children when the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees against them, he seeks mercy and righteousness for them. 

The secret of "And the Lord of Hosts is exalted through justice" is followed by: "and the Holy God is sanctified through righteousness." This means that when Justice is exalted, the judgment is put to rest and turns toward the attribute of <term>El</term> <gloss>God</gloss>, which is a secret, as it is said: "and the Holy God is sanctified through righteousness." In general, when "The Lord of Hosts is exalted through justice," the attribute of *El* comes from above and performs righteousness, and the judgment is sweetened. This is the secret of what they said: Justice is included in Loving-kindness and Judgment, and it says, "You have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob." The great secret is: "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne." For "Righteousness" <note>original: "צדק" (Tzedek)</note> is at times judgment, according to how it receives the flow, as I explained that *Tzedek* is a great, strong judgment. But when Justice is associated with it, then the Throne is established in Mercy. And if it is exalted through Justice, and reaches until Loving-kindness and Truth together—which are called the "Shining Countenance"—then everything becomes great mercies. IN the months of April and May of the year 1716, an abundance of haddock was brought into our city, coming to us from the seaside villages of Katwijk, Scheveningen, and Ter Heij. Many of these were still fresh, which we call <term>krimpschelvis</term> <gloss>twitching haddock; a term for very fresh fish that still retain muscle movement</gloss>, and for some days they were so cheap that they were bought for less than a <term>stuiver</term> <gloss>a small Dutch coin</gloss> apiece. And such has also happened a few years ago.

Reflecting on the multitude of these very tasty haddock, which were being caught at that time with nets, whereas they are otherwise caught with bait placed on a fishhook, I imagined that there must be a reason why the small haddock approached our sea coasts in such abundance, since a month or two later, not a single haddock was caught on our coasts.

I imagined that the abundance of the small haddock was dependent upon the bait or food that they were finding on our sea coasts.

II. It must next be considered that every single person from the multitude (so that a beginning may be made in establishing the commonwealth) must agree with the others, so that in those matters which are proposed by anyone in the assembly, that which the majority of them wills is held to be the will of all. For I have already seen the kingdoms, which are an allusion to the seven kingdoms. And so, "What are these" <note>clarification: referring to the horses in the vision</note> is a matter of my life within them.

The angel answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of heaven, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one with the black horses goes out toward the north country, and the white horses go out after them, and the dappled horses go out toward the south country." Then the strong horses went out and sought to go and walk to and fro throughout the earth, and he said, "Go, walk to and fro throughout the earth." So they walked to and fro throughout the earth. Then he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying, "See, those who go toward the north country have given rest to my spirit in the north country."

**The angel answered.** "These are the four winds." This is like saying "to the four winds." Similarly, "and he came Jerusalem" is like "to Jerusalem." Another interpretation: the letter <term>bet</term> in "with the black" <note>original: "בשחור"</note> is like the letter <term>lamed</term>, "to the black," and similar cases. This means He divided the four chariots and they go out to the four winds of heaven. This is to give authority to the four kingdoms to rule in the four winds, each one in its own time. This refers to the whole world, which is a place of strength. "From standing before the Lord of all the earth." This means they go as messengers of God, who gave them dominion over this. It is like the verse, "The sons of God came to stand before the Lord." <margin>Job 2</margin>

**The one with.** The black horses. He mentions the black ones because the time of the kingdom of Babylon had already passed. The kingdom of Media and Persia first went toward the north country, as they were meant to destroy it, and afterward they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. "And the white horses," which are the kingdom of Greece <note>original: "מלכות יון"</note>, went out after them as that kingdom emerged. For Alexander of Macedon <note>original: "אלכסנדרוס מקדון"</note>, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him, and he and the kings after him ruled throughout the entire world.

**And the dappled horses go out toward the south country.** This refers to the Roman part <note>clarification: the Roman Empire</note>, for Rome is in the north, as proven by the Caesar who ruled over Rome. He began to fight against the kingdom of Greece, and at the beginning of his wars, he went out toward the land of Egypt, which is in the south. At that time, the Greeks ruled in all lands, but Caesar grew strong against them and transferred the kingdom from the Greeks and restored it to the Romans.

**And the strong horses.** These are an allusion to the kingdom of Ishmael <note>context: traditionally identified with the Islamic Caliphates</note>, who exerted themselves of their own accord to seek a kingdom, to find a place for themselves to settle. This is why it says, "and they sought to go and walk to and fro throughout the earth."

**And he said.** Meaning, He gave them permission to walk about and conquer lands.

**Then he cried out.** Meaning, he called to me with a loud voice and said to me: **"See, those who go toward the north country have given rest to my spirit in the north country."** This refers to the black horses that went out toward Babylon to destroy it.

However, certain superstitious people and children of this age, wishing to heap errors upon errors, attempt to defend themselves beyond the understanding and intention of <term>Scotus</term> <gloss>John Duns Scotus, a Scholastic theologian</gloss> and the canonists with these arguments. They say that natural things have certain hidden virtues for which a reason cannot be assigned by man, just as a magnet attracts iron. And there are many other things that <term>Augustine</term> <gloss>Saint Augustine of Hippo</gloss> enumerates in book twenty-one of *The City of God* <note>original: "de civitate dei"</note>. Therefore, they argue, methods for health should be included where exorcisms and natural medicines fail. It would not be illicit, they claim, if one were to seek health for oneself or another through images that are not <term>necromantic</term> <gloss>divination through the dead</gloss> or astrological, or through rings and things of that sort.

They also argue: just as natural bodies are subject to celestial bodies, so too artificial bodies, such as images, acquire certain hidden virtues following the impression of celestial bodies. Therefore, artificial bodies, such as images, also acquire some hidden virtues from celestial bodies to cause certain effects, and so using them and others of this kind is not illicit. Furthermore, demons can transmute bodies in many ways, as <term>Augustine</term> says in book three of *On the Trinity* <note>original: "de trinitate"</note>, and this is evident in those afflicted by witchcraft. Therefore, it is permitted to use even their power to remove those afflictions.

But in truth, the words of all holy doctors are to the contrary, and this has been made clear in various places. Hence, regarding the first point, he says that if natural things are simply applied to produce some effects for which they are thought to have a natural virtue, it is not illicit. If, however, they add any characters or other unknown things and vain observations which manifestly do not possess such efficacy naturally, it will be superstitious and illicit, as <term>Thomas</term> <gloss>Thomas Aquinas</gloss> discusses in the *Summa Theologica*, part two of the second part, question ninety-six, article two, at the end of the question <note>original: "Tho. ii. ii. q. xcvi. ar. ii. in pede questionis"</note>.

<margin>By this same vessel they use the heart and tongue of Egypt.</margin>
The divine water-vessel, or that which causes water to gush upon heaven and earth, is depicted by a water-vessel resembling a heart with a tongue. It is compared to a heart because the heart is the ruling part of the body among them, just as the Nile is the ruler of Egypt. It is compared to a tongue because the tongue is always in a state of moisture and they call it the generator of what is good. They use two water-vessels, neither more nor less, because the action of the rising <note>clarification: of the river</note> is twofold according to them. They place one for the land of Egypt, since Egypt is by itself a generator of water; they place the other for the Ocean, for from it water comes to Egypt at the time of the inundation. They also attribute it to the rains which occur in the southern parts of Ethiopia at the time of the Nile's rising. That Egypt itself generates water can be learned from this: in the rest of the world's climates, the floods of rivers are completed during the winter.

### Chapter 3: Examination of Intentions

Even when an approach is made, women who are firm or bold must be tested. Since such women do not easily reveal their true disposition, and a special approach cannot be made without knowing it, the examination of intentions <term>Bhava-pariksha</term> is now described:

While making his approach, the suitor should observe the woman's conduct; by doing so, her intentions are tested.

<margin>Just as one approaches a maiden, he should observe her conduct, meaning her gestures and movements. By observing these, her inner disposition is examined.</margin>

How is she to be won? He says:

If she does not disclose her secret thoughts, he should win her over through a female messenger.

<margin>If she does not disclose her secret thoughts, meaning she does not reveal her feelings regarding a sexual union, he should employ a female messenger because the woman is bold.</margin>

If she rejects the initial approach but continues to associate with him, he should know that her mind is divided; he should win her over gradually.

<margin>If she rejects the approach made by the hero but, after a few days have passed, she is found associating or seeking contact with him again, he should recognize that her mind is divided. Because she needs to be tested, she feels "I do not know what I should do." He should win her over gradually and not abandon her in haste.</margin>

Regarding this, he states a specific detail:

If she rejects the approach but appears again wearing more elaborate ornaments, then in the same manner...

### Explanation of that Hadith of Mustafa <note>context: The Prophet Muhammad</note>, peace be upon him: "Indeed, God Almighty created the angels and placed intellect in them; He created the beasts and placed desire in them; and He created the children of Adam and placed both intellect and desire in them. He whose intellect overcomes his desire is higher than the angels, and he whose desire overcomes his intellect is lower than the beasts." The Messenger of God spoke the truth.

<column-break/>

God the Glorious created the world's creatures in three ways. One group is predominantly intellect, knowledge, and generosity; that is the angel, who knows nothing but prostration. There is no greed or passion in their element; they are absolute light, living by the love of God. Another group is void of knowledge, like animals finding beauty in fodder. They think of nothing but the stable and feed; out of wretchedness they are wise, and void of honor. This third kind is the child of Adam and human; half of him is inclined toward the higher realm, while the other half—the donkey—is inclined toward the lower. These two <note>clarification: the angels and the beasts</note> groups are at rest from war and strife, but humans are divided into three communities through trial. One group has become absolutely submerged, joined with the angels like Jesus. They are released from anger, passion, and idle talk; they have the form of a man but the meaning of Gabriel. They are freed from spiritual discipline, asceticism, and struggle. The other group has joined with the beasts; they have become pure anger and absolute desire. The house of the body was narrow and that Gabriel-like quality in them was lost. He made them dead, like a person who is soulless, for the soul that does not have the Beloved is base. Such a one lives a life lower than the animals. The deception and trickery he knows how to weave, the weaving of gold-embroidered robes, the finding of pearls in the depths of the sea, along with astronomy, medicine, and philosophy—these have no path to the seventh heaven. All of this relates to the stable <note>clarification: the material world</note>, for this science is the pillar of the beast's life. They gave these things names like "secrets of the universe," but the goal is merely the preservation of the animal for a few days.

Now it is said that after Xiangling had met everyone and finished her evening meal, and while Baochai and the others went to Madam Wang's <note>clarification: the text refers to her as "Aunt," the mother of Baochai</note> quarters, she went alone to the Bamboo Lodge <note>original: "瀟湘館" (Xiaoxiang Guan)</note>. At this time, Daiyu was mostly recovered. Seeing that Xiangling had also entered the garden to live, she was naturally pleased. Xiangling said with a smile, "Now that I have come in and have some free time, if you would teach me how to compose poetry, it would be my great good fortune!" Daiyu smiled and said, "If you want to learn to write poetry, you must take me as your teacher. Although I am not truly proficient, I can generally manage to teach you." Xiangling laughed, "If that is really so, I shall take you as my teacher, and you must not grow weary of me." Daiyu said, "What is so difficult about it that it is worth such concern? It is nothing more than the introduction, development, transition, and conclusion <note>original: "起承轉合" (qi cheng zhuan he)</note>. Within the development and transition, there are two pairs of couplets: level tones against oblique tones, and empty words against solid words, or solid against empty. If you truly have a remarkable line, it is acceptable even if the tones and the balance of words do not match perfectly."

Xiangling laughed, "No wonder when I used to secretly look at one or two poems in an old book, some were perfectly balanced while others were not. I also heard people say, 'the first, third, and fifth syllables do not matter, but the second, fourth, and sixth must be distinct.' Looking at the poems of the ancients, some followed this while others were wrong on the second, fourth, or sixth syllables. I was confused every day. Now hearing you speak, it seems these rules are actually of no consequence, as long as the phrasing is novel and original." Daiyu said, "That is exactly the principle. Phrasing is ultimately a secondary matter; the most important thing is the conception <note>original: "立意" (liyi)</note>. If the intent and interest are genuine, the poem will be good even without polishing the words. This is what is called 'not letting the words damage the meaning'."

Xiangling said, "I only love Lu Fangweng's <note>context: the Southern Song dynasty poet Lu You</note> lines: 'The heavy curtains are not rolled up, keeping the fragrance long; the ancient ink-slab is slightly concave, gathering much ink.' It is so vivid and interesting!" Daiyu said, "Because you do not understand poetry, you love what is shallow and accessible. Once you enter that pattern, you will never be able to break out of it. Listen to me: if you truly want to learn, I have the *Complete Works of Wang Mojie* <note>context: the Tang dynasty poet Wang Wei</note> here. Take a hundred of his five-syllable regulated poems and study them until you have mastered them thoroughly. Then read one hundred and twenty of Old Du's <note>context: the poet Du Fu</note> seven-syllable regulated poems, and after that, one or two hundred of Li Qinglian's <note>context: the poet Li Bai</note> seven-syllable quatrains. Once you have these three people as a foundation in your mind, you can then look at Tao Yuanming, Ying, Liu, Xie, Ruan, Yu, Bao, and the others. Since you are such an intelligent and clever person, in less than a year's time, you need not worry about becoming a true poet!" Hearing this, Xiangling smiled, "If that is so, good Miss, please bring that book out for me. I will take it back and it will be good to read a few poems at night." Hearing this, Daiyu ordered Zijuan to bring the five-syllable regulated poems of Wang the Right Chancellor <note>context: another title for Wang Wei</note> and handed them to Xiangling, saying, "Only look at those with red circles; those are the ones I have selected. Read them one by one. If there is something you do not understand, ask your mistress <note>clarification: Baochai</note>, or if you run into me, I will explain it to you."

Xiangling took the poems and returned to the Garden of Plantain Marvels <note>original: "蘅蕪院" (Hengwu Yuan)</note>. Neglecting all other matters, she began to read poem after poem under the lamp. Baochai urged her several times to go to sleep, but she would not. Seeing her such heart-felt devotion, Baochai had to let her be.

One day, just as Daiyu had finished washing and dressing, she saw Xiangling coming in with a beaming face to return the book, asking to exchange it for the poems of Du Fu. Daiyu smiled and asked, "How many do you remember?" Xiangling laughed, "I have read all of those marked with red circles." Daiyu asked, "Have you gained any understanding of them?" Xiangling smiled and said, "I have indeed gained some understanding, but I do not know if it is correct. Let me tell it to you."

A king entrusted his son to a tutor <term>adib</term> <gloss>a teacher of literature and ethics</gloss>, saying, "Educate my son as you have educated one of your own." The tutor labored for several years, and the result was that his own children reached the heights of knowledge, while the prince did not. The King summoned the scholar and rebuked him, saying, "You have broken your promise and failed to fulfill the conditions." The tutor replied: 

"O Lord of the Earth, let it not remain hidden from your enlightened mind that although the education is the same, natures are different." **Poem**

Though silver and gold come out of stone,
They are not found in every stone.

# The Reason We Set the Distance

We have set the distance from the point of midday <note>original: "نصف النهار"</note> because the adjustment <note>term: ta‘dīl</note> <gloss>correction or astronomical adjustment</gloss> for a birth is easier by this method than by working with horizons. The longest daylight hours for the latitude of Jerusalem <note>original: "بيت المقدس"</note> are fourteen hours and a fraction. Therefore, the Jewish method of using seasonal hours <note>term: al-sā‘āt al-zamāniyyah</note> <gloss>unequal hours that divide daylight and night into twelve parts regardless of season</gloss> is only valid if the conjunction for the start of Tishrei <note>clarification: the Jewish New Year</note> coincides exactly with the autumnal equinox. However, it never coincides exactly with it, but precedes or follows it by a significant amount, as we have explained previously.

When we extract the time of the conjunction using the calculation provided by the Jews in the table we analyzed according to their view, we progress from that to knowing the first day of the year and determining its character: whether it is deficient, regular, or complete. We already know whether the year is an ordinary year <note>term: basīṭah</note> or a leap year <note>term: kabīsah</note>. We then look in the Table of Limits for a duration of days of the week whose two boundaries contain the time we found for the conjunction. We look on the leap year side if it is a leap year, and on the ordinary year side if it is an ordinary year. Once we find it, we find alongside it the day of the week for the start of the year and its character. When we know the start of the year and its character, and combine that character with its status as an ordinary or leap year, we can determine from this when the start of the following year will occur.
